Subject: Traffic capacity safeguard notice — FastStart public launch (temporary uplift request)

Team —

FastStart goes public with their 1.0 tomorrow EOD PST. They just shared an updated traffic plan (attached) that shows a 6x spike compared to the last week and a projected peak of ~18k requests/min (average token churn ~420k tokens/min) during a three-hour window at launch. They want to avoid early throttling and have asked if we can provide a temporary ingress uplift / rate ceiling increase for the 72-hour launch window.

Ask: can we provision a short-lived uplift (configurable per-route) and what product changes/constraints do you need from FastStart to keep this safe for other tenants? Specifically:
- Maximum acceptable burst (QPS or tokens/min) we can allow on a hosted route without breaking latency SLOs
- Any model pinning or smaller max-length settings we should require to reduce KV/cache churn
- Whether we need a canary ramp (recommended) and suggested cadence

I've attached their traffic plan (FastStart_traffic_plan_v3.pdf). Monica, do you have the final signed launch date and any commercial ask (credits/discount) from them? Marcus/Karthik — can you confirm feasibility and any infra ops steps (pre-warm cache, routing change, temp dedicated capacity)?

I want a short operational checklist we can hand to SRE and a single-approval path so we can respond within 2 hours.

Thanks —
Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

On Mon, Aug 9, 2026 at 9:12 AM Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team —
> FastStart goes public with their 1.0 tomorrow EOD PST...

Quick read — we can support a temporary uplift but need concrete limits and trade-offs spelled out. From product/runtime side:
- We can provide an ingress uplift to their hosted route up to ~25k req/min for an isolated 72-hour window if we:
  1) pin the model variant to a lower max-length profile (recommended max_tokens_per_request = 1024)
  2) pre-warm KV cache for the top ~10% prefixes (we'll need their representative prompt corpus)
  3) enable temporary routing to a burst pool (adds cost; will be billed)
- If they insist on unbounded length, latency risk increases; we'll enforce per-request token cap.
- Need SRE to add a temporary circuit-breaker (auto-throttle at 30k req/min) and to monitor tail latency.

Operational asks for the customer:
- Provide a 5000-item sample of production prompts for cache prewarm by 15:00 PST today
- Confirm whether the launch will be staged (canary ramp) or all-at-once — staged is strongly preferred

If those are acceptable I can draft the short approval template and the runtime changes. Marcus — can SRE stand this up if we get sign-off?

-Karthik
Head of Product, Serving Runtime

1) Operational constraints (customer must accept):
   - Per-request token cap: 1,024 tokens (enforced at LB)
   - Model pinned to "rwd-small-1.3b-1024" variant for the uplift window
   - Canary ramp required: 25% / 50% / 100% over 30-minute intervals; if customer opens all-at-once we will still allow it but will enable stricter circuit-breaking parameters

   - Pre-warm KV cache for top prefixes (need their 5k sample before 12:30 PST to start pre-warm)
   - Create burst routing to temporary capacity pool and enable auto-throttle at 30k req/min
   - Add tracing hooks and a short dashboard (token burn + tail latency + 95/99th percentiles)
3) Commercial / approvals:
   - Sales must approve the temporary billing uplift (cost pass-through). Please complete temp_quota_form.xlsx and attach the HubSpot deal link.
   - If customer requests launch credit, route to revenue ops for approval — Marcus will include impact estimate.

I'll attach the temp_quota_form.xlsx and the brief ops checklist. If we get the prompt corpus and the signed form by 18:00 PST today we can enable the uplift starting 02:00 PST tomorrow.
